settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic K-armed bandit with arbitrary model D (lower bound)

settings.definition_quote: We consider a bandit model $\mathcal{D}$, i.e., a collection of possible distributions $\nu_a$ associated with the arms.

settings.name_in_paper: Sub-Gaussian K-armed bandit with known mu*
settings.definition_quote: We consider the sub-Gaussian framework described in Section~\ref{sec:other-blb} and restrict our attention to the case when $\mu^\star$ is known.

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic K-armed bandit with well-behaved model D (lower bound)
unmapped: model D well-behaved: K_inf locally Lipschitz in its second argument (Definition eq:wbm)
settings.definition_quote:
A model $\mathcal{D}$ is well behaved if there exist two functions ... such that ... $\Kinf(
u_a,x+\eps,\cD) \leq \Kinf(
u_a,x,\cD) + \eps \, \omega_{\cD}(
u_a,x)$.

algorithms.name: Algorithm with bounded regret, thanks to the knowledge of mu* (Algorithm 1)

conditions: a is a suboptimal arm
strategy is uniformly fast convergent on D

source.label: th:asympt
source.quote: For all models $\mathcal{D}$, for all uniformly fast convergent strategies $\psi$ on $\cD$, for all bandit problems $\unu$, for all suboptimal arms $a$, \[ \liminf_{T \to \infty} \frac{\E_{\unu}[N_{\psi,a}(T)]}{\ln T} \geq \frac{1}{\Kinf(\nu_a,\mu^\star,\cD)}. \]

results.notes: Bound on expected pull count of suboptimal arm a (quantity other). Re-derivation of Burnetas-Katehakis bound, claimed without extra conditions on D. Theorem number not printed; inferred.

conditions: strategy is smarter than the uniform strategy on D (E[N_{a*}(T)] >= T/K for optimal arms)

source.label: th:2
source.quote: For all models $\cD$, for all strategies $\psi$ that are smarter than the uniform strategy on $\cD$, for all bandit problems~$\unu$, for all arms $a$, for all $T \geq 1$, \[ \E_{\unu}[N_{\psi,a}(T)] \geq \frac{T}{K}(1 - \sqrt{2 T \Kinf(\nu_a,\mu^\star,\cD)}). \]

results.notes: Pull-count lower bound for arm a; regret lower bound via R = sum Delta_a E[N_a].

conditions: strategy is smarter than the uniform strategy on D

bound.regime: either E[N_a(T)] >= T/K, or this bound on the ratio holds

conditions: strategy pairwise symmetric for optimal arms on D
a suboptimal, a* optimal; KL_i = KL(nu_a, nu_{a*})

source.label: th:3
source.quote: For all models $\cD$, for all strategies $\psi$ that are pairwise symmetric for optimal arms on $\cD$, ... for all $T \geq 1$, either $\E_{\unu}[N_{\psi,a}(T)] \geq \frac{T}{K}$ or $\E_{\unu}[\frac{\max\{N_{\psi,a}(T),1\}}{\max\{N_{\psi,a^\star}(T),1\}}] \geq 1 - 2\sqrt{\frac{2T\KL(\nu_a,\nu_{a^\star})}{K}}$.

results.notes: Disjunctive statement; only the ratio branch recorded as expression, the alternative branch noted in regime. Bounds an expected ratio of pull counts.

bound.regime: T <= K/(32*KL_i); either E[N_a(T)] >= T/K or the ratio bound holds

conditions: strategy pairwise symmetric for optimal arms on D
results.notes: Disjunctive statement on an expected ratio of pull counts.

symbols.A_star: number of optimal arms of the instance
symbols.K_max: min over worst arms w of max over optimal arms a* of KL(nu_w, nu_{a*})

conditions: strategy pairwise symmetric for optimal arms and monotonic on D

source.label: th:4
source.quote: For all models $\cD$, for all strategies $\psi$ that are pairwise symmetric for optimal arms and monotonic on $\cD$, for all bandit problems $\unu$ in $\cD$, suboptimal arms are collectively sampled at least $\sum_{a \not\in \cA^\star(\unu)} \E_{\unu}[N_{\psi,a}(T)]\geq T(1-\frac{A^\star_{\unu}}{K} -\frac{A^\star_{\unu}\sqrt{2T\cK^{\max}_{\unu}}}{K}-\frac{2A^\star_{\unu}T\cK^{\max}_{\unu}}{K})$

results.notes: Collective pull-count bound; regret >= Delta_min times this (eq LBth4).

symbols.A_star: number of optimal arms of the instance
symbols.K_max: min over worst arms w of max over optimal arms a* of KL(nu_w, nu_{a*})

conditions: strategy pairwise symmetric for optimal arms and monotonic on D

bound.regime: T >= 2 with (ln T)^{-4} < eps_D(mu*) and a_T, b_T, c_T all < 1

symbols.omega: omega_D(nu_a, mu*), local Lipschitz constant of K_inf in the well-behaved definition
symbols.C_psi: constant C_{psi,D} of uniform super-fast convergence

conditions: strategy uniformly super-fast convergent: E[N_a(T)] <= C_psi ln T / Delta_a^2 for all instances, T >= 2
model D well-behaved
a suboptimal arm

source.label: th:LBlargeT-NA
source.quote: For all uniformly super-fast convergent strategies $\psi$ on well-behaved models $\mathcal{D}$, for all bandit problems $\unu$ in $\mathcal{D}$, for all suboptimal arms $a$, $\E_{\unu}[N_{\psi,a}(T)] \geq \frac{\ln T}{\Kinf(\nu_a,\mu^\star,\cD)}(1 - (a_T + b_T + c_T)) - \frac{\ln 2}{\Kinf(\nu_a,\mu^\star,\cD)}$, for all $T \geq 2$ large enough so that $(\ln T)^{-4} < \varepsilon_{\cD}(\mu^\star)$ and ...

results.notes: Second-order term is -O(ln ln T) per remark. Theorem number inferred.

conditions: instance nu_Delta = (N(0,1), N(-Delta,1))
strategy symmetric on nu_0 = (N(0,1),N(0,1)): E[N_1(T)] = E[N_2(T)] = T/2
sigma = 1

source.label: th:LB-BPR
source.quote: For all strategies $\psi$ that are symmetric in the sense of~\eqref{eq:sym}, for all $\Delta > 0$, for all $T \geq 1$, $\E_{\unu_{\Delta}}[N_{\psi,2}(T)] \geq \frac{1}{\Delta^2 + 1/T}$ and $R_{\psi,\unu_{\Delta},T} \geq \frac{\Delta}{\Delta^2 + 1/T}$.

results.notes: Well-chosen instance lower bound; also gives pull count bound 1/(Delta^2+1/T). Theorem number uncertain.

conditions: instance nu_Delta = (N(0,1), N(-Delta,1))
T such that E[N_2(T)] >= 1
sigma = 1

source.label: th:LB-BPR
source.quote: In addition, for all strategies $\psi$ and for all $T$ such that $\E_{\unu_{\Delta}}[N_{\psi,2}(T)] \geq 1$, ... $R_{\psi,\unu_{\Delta},T} \geq \min\{ \frac{2 (\ln 2) \Delta}{\Delta^2 + 2 \ln(4T)/T}, \frac{T\Delta}{2} \}$.

results.notes: Holds for all strategies, under condition on E[N_2(T)] >= 1.

conditions: max over the two instances (N(0,1),N(-Delta,1)) and (N(0,1),N(Delta,1))
sigma = 1

source.label: th:LB-BPR2
source.quote: Then, for all strategies $\psi$, for all $T \geq 1$, \max\{R_{\psi,\unu_1,T}, R_{\psi,\unu_2,T}\} \geq \min\{\frac{W(T \Delta^2/1.2)}{2 \Delta}, \frac{T\Delta}{2}\}.

results.notes: Minimax-type over two instances with known gap. Improves on BPR Theorem 6 for small T.

conditions: strategy symmetric and invariant by translation of the payoffs
sigma = 1

source.label: th:LB-BPR2
source.quote: Or, alternatively, for all strategies $\psi$ that are symmetric and invariant by translation of the payoffs, for all $T \geq 1$, $R_{\psi,\unu_1,T} = R_{\psi,\unu_2,T} \geq \frac{W(T \Delta^2/1.2)}{2 \Delta}$.

conditions: each arm 1-sub-Gaussian (sigma = 1)

source.label: th:finiteRegret:mus:known
source.quote: For all bandit problems $\unu = (\nu_a)_{a = 1,\ldots,K}$ where each distribution $\nu_a$ is sub-Gaussian in the sense of~\eqref{eq:sub-Gaussian}, the regret of the algorithm above is bounded by $R_{\unu,T} \leq \sum_{a : \Delta_a > 0} ( \frac{36\ln(17/\Delta_a)}{\Delta_a} + 3\Delta_a )$.

results.notes: Bounded (T-independent) regret; algorithm needs mu*, no T. Refinement of BPR results.
